entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 3 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 0 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). An exit is the finish of the last op of a completed traversal on the one timeline, so the beat is a difference of two timeline readings and never a max-stage-time formula (A1, P4 3).

entries.label: steady throughput = 1 / beat (HEADLINE)
entries.basis: D29's identity, on the measured beat: the pipeline is always full, so exactly ONE token leaves the last stage per beat and the system rate is 1/beat. The beat is the median of the SETTLED TAIL (3 interval(s)) of the 4 measured inter-exit intervals; the fill transient and any still-ramping intervals are held out and printed beside it, and this headline is only a settled measurement when pipeline.beat_converged is true — the run says so by name when it is not. Nothing here is a period times a count.

entries.label: per-stream token rate
entries.basis: 1 / (D x beat) with D = 64 resident streams (D29). A stream gets the machine once every D beats, which is the price of keeping the pipeline full.

entries.label: resident streams D (= pipeline stages)
entries.basis: the stage count, DERIVED from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip). D29 makes D a consequence of the stage plan, never a configured batch — the serving surface refuses a batch by name.

entries.label: per-token latency (one stream's traversal of the pipeline)
entries.basis: finish of traversal 4's last op minus the issue of its first, both read off the one timeline: the wall time one stream needs to walk every stage and emit one token. D29's identity says this is D x beat; the identity residual is reported in the pipeline block rather than replacing the measurement.

disclosures.reason: A1 / D17: the fabric is fully-connected p2p, analytical. Boundary bytes are placed and reported; no queueing, routing or topology term exists anywhere in this mapping.

D17 declares one network law and it is the p2p fabric BETWEEN chips. Activations moving between macros of one chip are carried as DAG dependencies with their byte count annotated and no link charge: no on-chip interconnect law is declared anywhere, and inventing one would be a number no card supports.

This model is priced through the 'llama' carrier: model_type selects the FFN/attention arithmetic, not the model's identity. Owners, labels and the atlas all name 'Falcon-Mamba-7B'; the carrier is named here so the two spellings are reconciled and not read as a contradiction.

disclosures.value: filled_pipeline (D29): D = 32 resident streams, local batch 1
disclosures.reason: The pipeline is ALWAYS FULL. 32 PP stages from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip); D = the stage count, DERIVED and never configured as a batch (D29 removes batch size from this surface). Decode is independent streams staggered one stage apart: one token exits per BEAT, throughput = 1/beat, per-stream rate = 1/(D x beat), every analog op fires at M = 1 and attention/scan are priced per stream at that stream's own context. EVERY stage holds all D streams' state and KV for its layers, which the evaluation reports per stage and checks against the declared tiers.

disclosures.value: 36 beats lowered (31 to fill the pipeline, then 3 STEADY inter-exit intervals measured)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-6 bounds the lowered window; D29 makes the unit a BEAT. The pipeline needs D - 1 = 31 beats to fill; 5 traversals then complete inside the window and their 4 inter-exit intervals are measured, of which the FIRST is held out (that traversal travelled through a filling pipeline, so nothing queued behind it and its exit is early). The beat is the median of the remaining 3. The declared decode_len (256 tokens per request) never enters the DAG: a request's decode phase is decode_len x D x beat and the evaluation prints it in its extrapolation block, labeled.

disclosures.value: dense (Invariant W, D27): 3808 macros, global cell floor 2852, waste 25.117%
disclosures.reason: Every bank of every macro holds real weights; waste is the dimension-mismatch remainder (2256535552 cells) plus the unfilled tail of a last macro (0 cells), and nothing else. Dense packing reaches 3808 analog macros where the per-tensor placement reaches 3840: 32 macros of analog silicon that held no weights now hold some. The delta is stated here rather than left for a reader to notice. K stacks: 0 in-macro (one accumulator per macro under the k_inner walk) and 1856 spread across macros (priced by the existing row-block partial-sum law).

D12 sizes the per-macro digital pool so it NEVER BLOCKS the pipeline, and no card declares a per-element cost for a norm, an activation, a residual add or a short depthwise conv. These ops therefore carry zero time and zero energy, exactly as the pass-1/2 report's 'helper lanes are absorbed into their stage' assumption does. Their CONCURRENCY is still measured and it drives the derived pool width (P4.5), so 'absorbed' is a sized claim here, not a hope.

disclosures.value: priced with the shift-and-add tree law
disclosures.reason: A row-block partial sum and a bit-slice composition are the same adder tree on the same per-macro pool, so they are priced by the same P2 law (price_reduction) with the operand count in place of the slice count. Declaring a second law for one shape would be a second accounting (D21).

cim.cards.<card>.pool_energy_per_add_pj is 0, so the priced shift-add trees report zero energy rather than an invented per-add figure. The reduction TIME is fully priced; only its energy is uncovered (ADJ-4).

vector_lanes = 36864 is DERIVED (D31-v2, ADJ-9) to the ANALOG FLOOR: the smallest width for which every stage's digital per-stage time fits that stage's own measured ANALOG m-pass time, with no margin (D28). Stage 1 is binding at a 6.4e-07 s analog m-pass and the engine runs at 12.171% duty inside it; 32 of 32 stage(s) are analog-bound by construction.
vector_clock_ghz undeclared: inherited cim.fabric.clock_ghz = 0.95 GHz (one chiplet declares one clock).
vector_pipeline_depth undeclared: inherited cim.fabric.softmax_pipeline_depth = 20, the only elementwise-pipeline depth this chiplet declares.

state_bytes_per_cycle undeclared: recurrent-state traffic is REPORTED and bounds nothing. A scan whose state does not fit the engine's registers would be state-bound; this model cannot say so until a card declares the number (disclosed relaxation, not a silent zero).

disclosures.value: vector engine at 157.409 W (composed), charged for the op's own time
disclosures.reason: D32: the shared digital chiplet's energy is now COMPOSED from the measured synthesis library — the engine's block census times each block's own measured power gives 157.409 W, and an op is charged that power for exactly as long as it runs. The label is PARTIAL, not COVERED, and here is why: the library reports ONE average power per block and does not separate dynamic from static, so (a) a block's power is charged at its synthesis toggle rate rather than at this op's activity, and (b) the chiplet's LEAKAGE while it is idle is not charged at all — an idle engine costs 0 pJ here, which is a floor, not a measurement. Both directions are named rather than folded into one adjusted number (D21, one accounting per metric).

disclosures.value: vector_lanes = 36864 (derived-count), binding stage 1, engine duty 12.171% of that stage's own 6.4e-07 s ANALOG m-pass; 32 of 32 stage(s) analog-bound
disclosures.reason: D31-v2 (ADJ-9): the scan/vector engine is never a swept or declared free knob, and it is sized to the ANALOG FLOOR rather than to the beat. Its width is DERIVED here as the smallest integer lane count for which EVERY stage's digital per-stage time fits that stage's OWN measured analog m-pass time, with no margin (D28). Both targets come from a PROBE pass in which every vector op is counted and costs nothing, so nothing the engine is sized against depends on the engine. The derivation inverts CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work exactly, so the engine sized here is the engine the run is then priced on. THE CRITERION IS digital-per-stage <= the stage's ANALOG m-pass time: the analog side is the binding term by construction wherever it can be. It does not make the MEASURED beat equal the analog time and cannot — a D29 stage holds one stream at a time, so its analog passes and its scan run in series and the measured beat is their sum at any width (here 7.78947e-08 s of digital against a 6.4e-07 s analog m-pass on the binding stage). Per stage: stage 0: 74/608 cycles, digital 7.789e-08 s vs analog 6.4e-07 s, stage 1: 74/607 cycles, digital 7.789e-08 s vs analog 6.4e-07 s, stage 2: 74/607 cycles, digital 7.789e-08 s vs analog 6.4e-07 s, stage 3: 74/607 cycles, digital 7.789e-08 s vs analog 6.4e-07 s, stage 4: 74/607 cycles, digital 7.789e-08 s vs analog 6.4e-07 s, stage 5: 74/607 cycles, digital 7.789e-08 s vs analog 6.4e-07 s. Every stage's criterion was reachable.

disclosures.value: 32 of 32 stage(s) analog-bound after the derivation; the beat-setting stage 31 spends 1.6e-07 s on analog_macro/ssm_in_proj against 6.4e-07 s of analog m-pass
disclosures.reason: ADJ-9 asks the ANALOG side to be the binding term wherever that is physically reachable. The derivation guarantees the half it can: the DERIVED scan/vector engine is sized so its per-stage time fits inside that stage's own analog m-pass time. It cannot guarantee the other half on its own, because a stage also runs silicon D31 does not size. ADJ-10 then took the two that used to be DECLARED — the attention fabric's array count and the softmax pipeline's lane count — and derived them against this same per-stage target, so what is left underived is the array GEOMETRY (rows x cols) and the terms that are not engines. READ THIS ROW AS THE DERIVATION'S OWN INPUT, NOT AS THE MACHINE: it is measured on the PROBE pass, where the fabric still sits at its declared seed width. What binds the machine that gets BUILT is measured on the priced timeline and reported under its own name, evaluation.digital_silicon.binding_term. On the probe: the analog m-pass IS the largest term of the beat-setting stage. Terms (union of busy intervals, probe slice): analog_macro/ssm_in_proj 1.6e-07 s; analog_macro/ssm_dt_proj 1.6e-07 s; analog_macro/ssm_out_proj 1.6e-07 s; analog_macro/ssm_x_proj 1.6e-07 s; macro_pool/ssm_out_proj 8e-08 s. Stage span 8.29474e-07 s.

disclosures.value: probe beat 8.29474e-07 s, CONVERGED (3 settled interval(s), 0 dropped as ramp, whole steady sample spread 0.0000%)
disclosures.reason: The probe pass is where BOTH of ADJ-9's inputs are measured: each stage's analog m-pass time (the sizing target) and this beat (the fallback budget for a stage the criterion cannot reach). The beat is a measurement like any other, so this line is where a reader sees whether it settled. Under D31-v2 the beat no longer sizes any stage that has analog work, so a still-ramping beat can only move a FALLBACK row; the analog stage times themselves are sums of op durations and do not ramp. The beat is read off the same settled tail the priced pass uses (P7.9), so it does not move with the window.

D32: the derived engine's silicon is a COMPOSITION of measured synthesis blocks — FP_MULT x 36864, FP_ADD x 36864, M_REG x 36864 — at 22nm. 36864 lane(s) x (FP_MULT + FP_ADD + M_REG): one lane retires one scalar operation of EITHER kind per vector cycle, which is the peak CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work is bound to, so the lane holds both arithmetic units.

disclosures.value: stage 18 spends 1.6e-07 s on analog_macro/ssm_in_proj against 6.4e-07 s of analog m-pass (stage span 9.36667e-07 s)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-10 requires that whatever binds AFTER every composable digital engine has been derived be a REAL limit and be named. This row is that name, measured on the PRICED timeline — the machine that gets built, with the derived fabric, the derived softmax width and the derived scan engine all installed — so it is a different quantity from the probe's beat-setting evidence, which describes the machine the derivation ran against. THE ANALOG M-PASS IS THE LARGEST TERM of the beat-setting stage: this machine runs at the analog floor, which is what ADJ-9 and ADJ-10 were adjudicated to reach. Terms (union of busy intervals, priced slice): analog_macro/ssm_in_proj 1.6e-07 s; analog_macro/ssm_x_proj 1.6e-07 s; analog_macro/ssm_dt_proj 1.6e-07 s; analog_macro/ssm_out_proj 1.6e-07 s; macro_pool/ssm_out_proj 8e-08 s.

The hardware config declares ONE activation/SRAM tier size (tech_config.DRAM.size); no per-chip capacity field exists anywhere in the schema. The feasibility check therefore applies the declared size to each chip independently. It is a relaxation and it is disclosed rather than presented as a per-chip capacity the config does not contain.

inference.kvcache_type = cim_sram puts the KV cache in the same activation SRAM tier the replay's activations draw on, so the verdict is taken on the SUM. Under cim_dram the KV cache gets its own declared tier and its own verdict.

disclosures.value: on-chip 6.71089e+07 B (tech_param.SRAM-L2.size) applied to EVERY stage; the activation stub 8.58993e+09 B (tech_param.DRAM.size) reported beside it
disclosures.reason: The state/KV feasibility check needs a per-stage capacity and the schema declares no per-stage field. D29's state is RESIDENT and read every beat, so the tier that decides feasibility is the declared ON-CHIP SRAM-L2 size, and that is what state_residency.verdict is taken against; the DRAM activation stub is orders of magnitude larger and would make the check vacuous, so it rides under its own name as activation_tier_verdict rather than as the headline. Each declared size is applied to each stage independently, exactly as the per-chip verdicts apply theirs to each chip. A stage that spans several chips is judged against one chip's tier, which is PESSIMISTIC, and it is disclosed rather than silently scaled by a chip count the schema does not tie to a stage.

D29 leaves the resident streams at DIFFERENT decode depths. Every priced attention and scan op uses ITS OWN stream's context — no op is priced at the representative figure. The representative context is the MEDIAN over the lowered window and exists so a reader can name the depth the reported state figures belong to. The convention is: stream i enters at prefill_len + i + 1 and advances one token every D beats.

silicon.basis: 3568 enumerated analog macro slots x macro_footprint_mm2 2.02041 + 8 shared digital chiplets x the card's COMPOSED area 9.79413 mm2 (D32: measured 22nm synthesis blocks, unit counts x measured area, no overhead) + 3568 per-macro digital pools x the COMPOSED pool area 0.00241842 mm2 (D32, same measured library) + an on-chip state store of 2017 measured SRAM macro(s) = 106.914 mm2, SIZED to the 6.71089e+07 B of resident state this mapping holds. The analog term is the P3.6 atlas's enumerated_macro_silicon (slots the machine HAS), NOT CimDeviceModel.total_area_mm2 (arrays a model NEEDS).

packing.basis: D27's waste, counted in CELLS: committed cells that hold no real weight, over the committed total. cell_floor_macros is the GLOBAL lower bound ceil(total model cells / cells per macro); a per-chip packer cannot reach it when the layers are split across chips, so macros >= cell_floor_macros is expected and the gap is the price of the chip split, not a packing failure.

derived_chiplets.basis: REPORTED, NOT APPLIED. First-fit over the stages sorted heaviest-first, bounded by the beat: this is how few chiplets the digital work would fit on IF a chiplet's engines were sized for every stage it serves. They are sized per stage today, so the machine keeps one chiplet per stage and this row is the headroom that sizing leaves on the table.

pipeline.basis: D29: the pipeline is ALWAYS FULL. tokens/s = 1/beat is the exit rate of ONE token per beat; D = the stage count, DERIVED from the stage plan and never configured; the per-stream rate is 1/(D x beat).

state_bill.basis: D29: EVERY stage holds ALL D resident streams' state and KV for the layers it owns. The per-stage figure is the SAME per-(chip, layer) quantities the memory verdicts are taken on, regrouped by stage — not a second computation (D21): recurrent state is D x P2's per-stream state law, and KV is the SUM over the resident streams of P2's kv_bytes_per_stream_layer at each stream's OWN context, because the streams sit at different decode depths.

disclosures.reason: A1 / D17: the fabric is fully-connected p2p, analytical. Boundary bytes are placed and reported; no queueing, routing or topology term exists anywhere in this mapping.

D17 declares one network law and it is the p2p fabric BETWEEN chips. Activations moving between macros of one chip are carried as DAG dependencies with their byte count annotated and no link charge: no on-chip interconnect law is declared anywhere, and inventing one would be a number no card supports.

This model is priced through the 'llama' carrier: model_type selects the FFN/attention arithmetic, not the model's identity. Owners, labels and the atlas all name 'Falcon-Mamba-7B'; the carrier is named here so the two spellings are reconciled and not read as a contradiction.

disclosures.value: filled_pipeline (D29): D = 4 resident streams, local batch 1
disclosures.reason: The pipeline is ALWAYS FULL. 4 PP stages from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip); D = the stage count, DERIVED and never configured as a batch (D29 removes batch size from this surface). Decode is independent streams staggered one stage apart: one token exits per BEAT, throughput = 1/beat, per-stream rate = 1/(D x beat), every analog op fires at M = 1 and attention/scan are priced per stream at that stream's own context. EVERY stage holds all D streams' state and KV for its layers, which the evaluation reports per stage and checks against the declared tiers.

disclosures.value: 8 beats lowered (3 to fill the pipeline, then 3 STEADY inter-exit intervals measured)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-6 bounds the lowered window; D29 makes the unit a BEAT. The pipeline needs D - 1 = 3 beats to fill; 5 traversals then complete inside the window and their 4 inter-exit intervals are measured, of which the FIRST is held out (that traversal travelled through a filling pipeline, so nothing queued behind it and its exit is early). The beat is the median of the remaining 3. The declared decode_len (256 tokens per request) never enters the DAG: a request's decode phase is decode_len x D x beat and the evaluation prints it in its extrapolation block, labeled.

disclosures.value: dense (Invariant W, D27): 3568 macros, global cell floor 2852, waste 20.080%
disclosures.reason: Every bank of every macro holds real weights; waste is the dimension-mismatch remainder (1690304512 cells) plus the unfilled tail of a last macro (0 cells), and nothing else. Dense packing reaches 3568 analog macros where the per-tensor placement reaches 3712: 144 macros of analog silicon that held no weights now hold some. The delta is stated here rather than left for a reader to notice. K stacks: 1376 in-macro (one accumulator per macro under the k_inner walk) and 2144 spread across macros (priced by the existing row-block partial-sum law).

D12 sizes the per-macro digital pool so it NEVER BLOCKS the pipeline, and no card declares a per-element cost for a norm, an activation, a residual add or a short depthwise conv. These ops therefore carry zero time and zero energy, exactly as the pass-1/2 report's 'helper lanes are absorbed into their stage' assumption does. Their CONCURRENCY is still measured and it drives the derived pool width (P4.5), so 'absorbed' is a sized claim here, not a hope.
cim.cards.<card>.pool_energy_per_add_pj is 0, so the K-stack accumulators report zero energy rather than an invented per-add figure. The accumulator TIME is fully priced (P7.2).

disclosures.value: priced with the shift-and-add tree law
disclosures.reason: A row-block partial sum and a bit-slice composition are the same adder tree on the same per-macro pool, so they are priced by the same P2 law (price_reduction) with the operand count in place of the slice count. Declaring a second law for one shape would be a second accounting (D21).

cim.cards.<card>.pool_energy_per_add_pj is 0, so the priced shift-add trees report zero energy rather than an invented per-add figure. The reduction TIME is fully priced; only its energy is uncovered (ADJ-4).

vector_lanes = 2370 is DERIVED (D31-v2, ADJ-9) to the ANALOG FLOOR: the smallest width for which every stage's digital per-stage time fits that stage's own measured ANALOG m-pass time, with no margin (D28). Stage 0 is binding at a 5.04e-06 s analog m-pass and the engine runs at 99.916% duty inside it; 4 of 4 stage(s) are analog-bound by construction.
vector_clock_ghz undeclared: inherited cim.fabric.clock_ghz = 0.95 GHz (one chiplet declares one clock).
vector_pipeline_depth undeclared: inherited cim.fabric.softmax_pipeline_depth = 20, the only elementwise-pipeline depth this chiplet declares.

state_bytes_per_cycle undeclared: recurrent-state traffic is REPORTED and bounds nothing. A scan whose state does not fit the engine's registers would be state-bound; this model cannot say so until a card declares the number (disclosed relaxation, not a silent zero).

disclosures.value: vector engine at 10.1199 W (composed), charged for the op's own time
disclosures.reason: D32: the shared digital chiplet's energy is now COMPOSED from the measured synthesis library — the engine's block census times each block's own measured power gives 10.1199 W, and an op is charged that power for exactly as long as it runs. The label is PARTIAL, not COVERED, and here is why: the library reports ONE average power per block and does not separate dynamic from static, so (a) a block's power is charged at its synthesis toggle rate rather than at this op's activity, and (b) the chiplet's LEAKAGE while it is idle is not charged at all — an idle engine costs 0 pJ here, which is a floor, not a measurement. Both directions are named rather than folded into one adjusted number (D21, one accounting per metric).

disclosures.value: vector_lanes = 2370 (derived-count), binding stage 0, engine duty 99.916% of that stage's own 5.04e-06 s ANALOG m-pass; 4 of 4 stage(s) analog-bound
disclosures.reason: D31-v2 (ADJ-9): the scan/vector engine is never a swept or declared free knob, and it is sized to the ANALOG FLOOR rather than to the beat. Its width is DERIVED here as the smallest integer lane count for which EVERY stage's digital per-stage time fits that stage's OWN measured analog m-pass time, with no margin (D28). Both targets come from a PROBE pass in which every vector op is counted and costs nothing, so nothing the engine is sized against depends on the engine. The derivation inverts CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work exactly, so the engine sized here is the engine the run is then priced on. THE CRITERION IS digital-per-stage <= the stage's ANALOG m-pass time: the analog side is the binding term by construction wherever it can be. It does not make the MEASURED beat equal the analog time and cannot — a D29 stage holds one stream at a time, so its analog passes and its scan run in series and the measured beat is their sum at any width (here 5.03579e-06 s of digital against a 5.04e-06 s analog m-pass on the binding stage). Per stage: stage 0: 4784/4788 cycles, digital 5.036e-06 s vs analog 5.04e-06 s, stage 1: 4784/4788 cycles, digital 5.036e-06 s vs analog 5.04e-06 s, stage 2: 4784/4788 cycles, digital 5.036e-06 s vs analog 5.04e-06 s, stage 3: 4784/4788 cycles, digital 5.036e-06 s vs analog 5.04e-06 s. Every stage's criterion was reachable.

disclosures.value: 4 of 4 stage(s) analog-bound after the derivation; the beat-setting stage 3 spends 1.28e-06 s on analog_macro/ssm_dt_proj against 5.04e-06 s of analog m-pass
disclosures.reason: ADJ-9 asks the ANALOG side to be the binding term wherever that is physically reachable. The derivation guarantees the half it can: the DERIVED scan/vector engine is sized so its per-stage time fits inside that stage's own analog m-pass time. It cannot guarantee the other half on its own, because a stage also runs silicon D31 does not size. ADJ-10 then took the two that used to be DECLARED — the attention fabric's array count and the softmax pipeline's lane count — and derived them against this same per-stage target, so what is left underived is the array GEOMETRY (rows x cols) and the terms that are not engines. READ THIS ROW AS THE DERIVATION'S OWN INPUT, NOT AS THE MACHINE: it is measured on the PROBE pass, where the fabric still sits at its declared seed width. What binds the machine that gets BUILT is measured on the priced timeline and reported under its own name, evaluation.digital_silicon.binding_term. On the probe: the analog m-pass IS the largest term of the beat-setting stage. Terms (union of busy intervals, probe slice): analog_macro/ssm_dt_proj 1.28e-06 s; analog_macro/ssm_in_proj 1.28e-06 s; analog_macro/ssm_out_proj 1.28e-06 s; analog_macro/ssm_x_proj 1.2e-06 s; macro_pool/ssm_in_proj 8e-07 s. Stage span 5.92842e-06 s.

disclosures.value: probe beat 5.92842e-06 s, CONVERGED (3 settled interval(s), 0 dropped as ramp, whole steady sample spread 0.0000%)
disclosures.reason: The probe pass is where BOTH of ADJ-9's inputs are measured: each stage's analog m-pass time (the sizing target) and this beat (the fallback budget for a stage the criterion cannot reach). The beat is a measurement like any other, so this line is where a reader sees whether it settled. Under D31-v2 the beat no longer sizes any stage that has analog work, so a still-ramping beat can only move a FALLBACK row; the analog stage times themselves are sums of op durations and do not ramp. The beat is read off the same settled tail the priced pass uses (P7.9), so it does not move with the window.

D32: the derived engine's silicon is a COMPOSITION of measured synthesis blocks — FP_MULT x 2370, FP_ADD x 2370, M_REG x 2370 — at 22nm. 2370 lane(s) x (FP_MULT + FP_ADD + M_REG): one lane retires one scalar operation of EITHER kind per vector cycle, which is the peak CimDeviceModel.price_vector_work is bound to, so the lane holds both arithmetic units.

disclosures.value: stage 3 spends 5.03579e-06 s on shared_digital/ssm_scan against 5.04e-06 s of analog m-pass (stage span 1.09642e-05 s)
disclosures.reason: ADJ-10 requires that whatever binds AFTER every composable digital engine has been derived be a REAL limit and be named. This row is that name, measured on the PRICED timeline — the machine that gets built, with the derived fabric, the derived softmax width and the derived scan engine all installed — so it is a different quantity from the probe's beat-setting evidence, which describes the machine the derivation ran against. THE NEXT REAL LIMIT is shared_digital/ssm_scan, which no ADJ-10 derivation sizes. Terms (union of busy intervals, priced slice): shared_digital/ssm_scan 5.036e-06 s; analog_macro/ssm_in_proj 1.28e-06 s; analog_macro/ssm_dt_proj 1.28e-06 s; analog_macro/ssm_out_proj 1.28e-06 s; analog_macro/ssm_x_proj 1.2e-06 s.

The hardware config declares ONE activation/SRAM tier size (tech_config.DRAM.size); no per-chip capacity field exists anywhere in the schema. The feasibility check therefore applies the declared size to each chip independently. It is a relaxation and it is disclosed rather than presented as a per-chip capacity the config does not contain.

inference.kvcache_type = cim_sram puts the KV cache in the same activation SRAM tier the replay's activations draw on, so the verdict is taken on the SUM. Under cim_dram the KV cache gets its own declared tier and its own verdict.

disclosures.value: on-chip 6.71089e+07 B (tech_param.SRAM-L2.size) applied to EVERY stage; the activation stub 8.58993e+09 B (tech_param.DRAM.size) reported beside it
disclosures.reason: The state/KV feasibility check needs a per-stage capacity and the schema declares no per-stage field. D29's state is RESIDENT and read every beat, so the tier that decides feasibility is the declared ON-CHIP SRAM-L2 size, and that is what state_residency.verdict is taken against; the DRAM activation stub is orders of magnitude larger and would make the check vacuous, so it rides under its own name as activation_tier_verdict rather than as the headline. Each declared size is applied to each stage independently, exactly as the per-chip verdicts apply theirs to each chip. A stage that spans several chips is judged against one chip's tier, which is PESSIMISTIC, and it is disclosed rather than silently scaled by a chip count the schema does not tie to a stage.

D29 leaves the resident streams at DIFFERENT decode depths. Every priced attention and scan op uses ITS OWN stream's context — no op is priced at the representative figure. The representative context is the MEDIAN over the lowered window and exists so a reader can name the depth the reported state figures belong to. The convention is: stream i enters at prefill_len + i + 1 and advances one token every D beats.

disclosures.value: analog_macro 0.572% mean / 0.704% peak (0 of 3568 idle), macro_pool 0.139% mean / 0.352% peak (736 of 3568 idle), shared_digital 17.996% mean / 44.299% peak (4 of 8 idle), link 1.183% mean / 1.183% peak (0 of 3 idle)
disclosures.reason: D28: idle silicon is a provisioning finding, never a fact to accept, so every device class prints its utilization on every run. The BINDING class here is shared_digital at 44.299% peak occupancy; a class far below it is silicon this provisioning does not need, and the system-sizing sweep is where that is fixed. No threshold decides when this banner appears — it always appears.

disclosures.value: 2720 local K stack(s) carry no accumulator op
disclosures.reason: A macro holds several K blocks of one output block, so their partials must be summed, but the placement that produced them is 'dense' and only the dense packer emits the KStack descriptor P7.2's accumulator law prices. The adds are therefore NOT in this timeline. Pack densely (mapping.packing: dense) to price them; the gap is disclosed rather than silently absorbed.

disclosures.value: 3 fill beats before 3 measured steady beats
disclosures.reason: D29's pipeline is full only after every stage has a stream, which takes D - 1 = 3 beats. The window lowers 8 beats: the fill is IN the DAG (its contention is priced like any other) and the beat is read from the exits of the completed traversals, whose intervals are printed one by one in the pipeline block so a reader can see the convergence rather than trust an average. Streams that enter too late to finish inside the window are lowered as far as the window reaches and their partial work is on the timeline, contending, exactly as it would in the machine.

DECODE_LEN x D x BEAT. A request occupies one stream and gets a token every D beats, so its decode phase is decode_len x D x beat. This is an EXTRAPOLATION — a period times a count — so it lives here, labeled, and never enters metrics[] (P4 3, ADJ-6). Prefill is not in it: D25/D29 make the mapped run decode-only and the streams arrive already prefilled.
P3 places; P4 prices (A1). Every op in the emitted DAG carries a zero duration and the annotation P4's pricing table needs. A number here would be a second accounting of a metric P4 owns (D21).

entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 3 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 0 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). An exit is the finish of the last op of a completed traversal on the one timeline, so the beat is a difference of two timeline readings and never a max-stage-time formula (A1, P4 3).

entries.label: steady throughput = 1 / beat (HEADLINE)
entries.basis: D29's identity, on the measured beat: the pipeline is always full, so exactly ONE token leaves the last stage per beat and the system rate is 1/beat. The beat is the median of the SETTLED TAIL (3 interval(s)) of the 4 measured inter-exit intervals; the fill transient and any still-ramping intervals are held out and printed beside it, and this headline is only a settled measurement when pipeline.beat_converged is true — the run says so by name when it is not. Nothing here is a period times a count.

entries.label: per-stream token rate
entries.basis: 1 / (D x beat) with D = 8 resident streams (D29). A stream gets the machine once every D beats, which is the price of keeping the pipeline full.

entries.label: resident streams D (= pipeline stages)
entries.basis: the stage count, DERIVED from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip). D29 makes D a consequence of the stage plan, never a configured batch — the serving surface refuses a batch by name.

entries.label: per-token latency (one stream's traversal of the pipeline)
entries.basis: finish of traversal 4's last op minus the issue of its first, both read off the one timeline: the wall time one stream needs to walk every stage and emit one token. D29's identity says this is D x beat; the identity residual is reported in the pipeline block rather than replacing the measurement.

extrapolation.basis: DECODE_LEN x D x BEAT. A request occupies one stream and gets a token every D beats, so its decode phase is decode_len x D x beat. This is an EXTRAPOLATION — a period times a count — so it lives here, labeled, and never enters metrics[] (P4 3, ADJ-6). Prefill is not in it: D25/D29 make the mapped run decode-only and the streams arrive already prefilled.

metrics.headline_basis: ADJ-6: tokens/s at the decode terminal, read off THIS candidate's own timeline (fws_eval.evaluate_fws over program.fws_build's placed DAG). No closed form and no period is involved anywhere in this row.

state_bill_summary.budget_basis: there is no residency budget. The on-chip state store is SIZED to each point's own measured per-stage bill, composed from integer copies of the measured SRAM macro and charged in silicon.state_sram_silicon_mm2, so holding state costs AREA and never refuses a point. The one feasibility budget is mapping_dse.max_silicon_mm2.
state_bill_summary.basis: D29: every stage holds ALL D streams' recurrent state and KV for its layers, so the per-stage bill scales with the resident-stream count D and D is the stage count. The bytes are fws_eval's own measured residency (evaluation.state_residency), not a second accounting.

entries.label: pipeline beat (one token exits per beat)
entries.basis: the MEDIAN of the SETTLED TAIL of the measured intervals between consecutive token exits: 3 of the 4 measured interval(s). One interval is held out as the traversal that entered at beat 0 and travelled through a filling pipeline (nothing queued behind it, so its exit lands early), and a further 0 interval(s) are dropped as RAMP because they do not agree with the tail's own median to 1e-03. Both sets are printed above rather than smoothed in, and the tail rule is what makes the reported beat independent of how many beats the window lowered (P7.9). An exit is the finish of the last op of a completed traversal on the one timeline, so the beat is a difference of two timeline readings and never a max-stage-time formula (A1, P4 3).

entries.label: steady throughput = 1 / beat (HEADLINE)
entries.basis: D29's identity, on the measured beat: the pipeline is always full, so exactly ONE token leaves the last stage per beat and the system rate is 1/beat. The beat is the median of the SETTLED TAIL (3 interval(s)) of the 4 measured inter-exit intervals; the fill transient and any still-ramping intervals are held out and printed beside it, and this headline is only a settled measurement when pipeline.beat_converged is true — the run says so by name when it is not. Nothing here is a period times a count.

entries.label: per-stream token rate
entries.basis: 1 / (D x beat) with D = 32 resident streams (D29). A stream gets the machine once every D beats, which is the price of keeping the pipeline full.

entries.label: resident streams D (= pipeline stages)
entries.basis: the stage count, DERIVED from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip). D29 makes D a consequence of the stage plan, never a configured batch — the serving surface refuses a batch by name.

entries.label: per-token latency (one stream's traversal of the pipeline)
entries.basis: finish of traversal 4's last op minus the issue of its first, both read off the one timeline: the wall time one stream needs to walk every stage and emit one token. D29's identity says this is D x beat; the identity residual is reported in the pipeline block rather than replacing the measurement.

extrapolation.basis: DECODE_LEN x D x BEAT. A request occupies one stream and gets a token every D beats, so its decode phase is decode_len x D x beat. metrics.headline_basis: ADJ-6: tokens/s at the decode terminal, read off THIS candidate's own timeline (fws_eval.evaluate_fws over program.fws_build's placed DAG). No closed form and no period is involved anywhere in this row.

The BINDING class here is shared_digital at 21.371% peak occupancy; a class far below it is silicon this provisioning does not need, and the system-sizing sweep is where that is fixed. No threshold decides when this banner appears — it always appears.

disclosures.value: 2784 local K stack(s) carry no accumulator op
disclosures.reason: A macro holds several K blocks of one output block, so their partials must be summed, but the placement that produced them is 'dense' and only the dense packer emits the KStack descriptor P7.2's accumulator law prices. The adds are therefore NOT in this timeline. Pack densely (mapping.packing: dense) to price them; the gap is disclosed rather than silently absorbed.

disclosures.value: 31 fill beats before 3 measured steady beats
disclosures.reason: D29's pipeline is full only after every stage has a stream, which takes D - 1 = 31 beats. The window lowers 36 beats: the fill is IN the DAG (its contention is priced like any other) and the beat is read from the exits of the completed traversals, whose intervals are printed one by one in the pipeline block so a reader can see the convergence rather than trust an average. Streams that enter too late to finish inside the window are lowered as far as the window reaches and their partial work is on the timeline, contending, exactly as it would in the machine.

DECODE_LEN x D x BEAT. A request occupies one stream and gets a token every D beats, so its decode phase is decode_len x D x beat. This is an EXTRAPOLATION — a period times a count — so it lives here, labeled, and never enters metrics[] (P4 3, ADJ-6). Prefill is not in it: D25/D29 make the mapped run decode-only and the streams arrive already prefilled.
P3 places; P4 prices (A1). Every op in the emitted DAG carries a zero duration and the annotation P4's pricing table needs. A number here would be a second accounting of a metric P4 owns (D21).

best_violation.fail_message: this point needs 23482.2 mm2 of silicon but mapping_dse.max_silicon_mm2 = 20000. Its terms: 7241.16 mm2 of analog weight macros + 14522.2 mm2 of shared digital chiplets + 8.66763 mm2 of per-macro pools + 1710.2 mm2 of on-chip state store (32264 measured SRAM macros sized to the state this mapping holds). Area is the one thing that refuses a machine here: holding more state costs silicon, it never makes a design infeasible.

disclosures.value: refused axes: arrays_per_chip, num_arrays, softmax_lanes, vector_lanes; the engine is DERIVED at every point
disclosures.reason: ADJ-13 retires the chip's SLOT COUNT as a swept or declared knob. A chip offers exactly the macro slots the layers it holds need, and that number is DERIVED from the placement itself: the sweep places the layers once to learn the requirement and builds the chip to it. Sweeping it produced garbage points at both ends — a capacity under the requirement is refused by the assembly check and tells you nothing, and a capacity over it enumerates empty slots that are charged as silicon, so the 'frontier' bought area with no throughput and called it a design point. What remains free is the PARTITION (layers_per_chip / layers_per_stage), which is a real choice; the capacity that partition implies is arithmetic.; ADJ-10 retires the attention fabric's ARRAY COUNT as a swept or declared knob, for the same reason D31/ADJ-9 retired the scan engine's lane count: it is a count of MEASURED synthesis blocks, so it is DERIVED — sized UP in integer copies of the measured GEMMINI 32x32 block until every stage's attention time fits that stage's own ANALOG m-pass time — and REPORTED (evaluation.digital_silicon.derived_fabric_sizing). Sweeping it would sweep the answer. Only the COUNT is derived: rows x cols per array stay as measured and as declared, because inventing array geometry is refused (ADJ-4). An explicit cim.cards.<card>.fabric_num_arrays on a SINGLE machine is still an OVERRIDE that rides its own disclosure; what is refused here is making it an AXIS.; ADJ-10 retires the softmax pipeline's LANE COUNT as a swept or declared knob on the same grounds as num_arrays: the lane is a MEASURED per-lane census (OPTIMA's softmax collection, block for block), so the width is DERIVED against the same per-stage analog m-pass target and REPORTED. cim.cards.<card>.fabric_softmax_lanes pins ONE machine with a disclosure; as an AXIS it is refused.; D31/ADJ-9 retire the scan/vector engine as a swept or declared knob: its width is DERIVED — sized UP until every stage's digital per-stage time fits that stage's own ANALOG m-pass time — and REPORTED (evaluation.digital_silicon.derived_engine_sizing). Sweeping it would sweep the answer. The frontier (P7.4) sweeps stage granularity, mux/bank depth and chip capacity, and derives the digital side at every point. An explicit cim.cards.<card>.vector_lanes on a single machine is still an OVERRIDE that rides its own disclosure (D31); what is refused here is making it an AXIS.

the ladder is a DIRECTIONAL walk from the declared initializer: it prices every point it steps to and every one-rung neighbour of those, and it never touches the rest of the cross product. The reported front is therefore the non-dominated set of the VISITED points and is a lower bound on the front of the whole declared space. Nothing unvisited is estimated, interpolated or sampled - it is simply absent, and the ladder trail says which steps the walk took and why it stopped.
A1 / D17: the fabric is fully-connected p2p, analytical. Boundary bytes are placed and reported; no queueing, routing or topology term exists anywhere in this mapping.

D17 declares one network law and it is the p2p fabric BETWEEN chips. Activations moving between macros of one chip are carried as DAG dependencies with their byte count annotated and no link charge: no on-chip interconnect law is declared anywhere, and inventing one would be a number no card supports.

This model is priced through the 'llama' carrier: model_type selects the FFN/attention arithmetic, not the model's identity. Owners, labels and the atlas all name 'Falcon-Mamba-7B'; the carrier is named here so the two spellings are reconciled and not read as a contradiction.

disclosures.value: filled_pipeline (D29): D = 16 resident streams, local batch 1
disclosures.reason: The pipeline is ALWAYS FULL. 16 PP stages from the chip partition (default: one stage per analog chip); D = the stage count, DERIVED and never configured as a batch (D29 removes batch size from this surface). Decode is independent streams staggered one stage apart: one token exits per BEAT, throughput = 1/beat, per-stream rate = 1/(D x beat), every analog op fires at M = 1 and attention/scan are priced per stream at that stream's own context. EVERY stage holds all D streams' state and KV for its layers, which the evaluation reports per stage and checks against the declared tiers.

disclosures.reason: The hardware config declares ONE activation/SRAM tier size (tech_config.DRAM.size); no per-chip capacity field exists anywhere in the schema. The feasibility check therefore applies the declared size to each chip independently. It is a relaxation and it is disclosed rather than presented as a per-chip capacity the config does not contain.

inference.kvcache_type = cim_sram puts the KV cache in the same activation SRAM tier the replay's activations draw on, so the verdict is taken on the SUM. Under cim_dram the KV cache gets its own declared tier and its own verdict.

disclosures.value: on-chip 6.71089e+07 B (tech_param.SRAM-L2.size) applied to EVERY stage; the activation stub 8.58993e+09 B (tech_param.DRAM.size) reported beside it
disclosures.reason: The state/KV feasibility check needs a per-stage capacity and the schema declares no per-stage field. D29's state is RESIDENT and read every beat, so the tier that decides feasibility is the declared ON-CHIP SRAM-L2 size, and that is what state_residency.verdict is taken against; the DRAM activation stub is orders of magnitude larger and would make the check vacuous, so it rides under its own name as activation_tier_verdict rather than as the headline. Each declared size is applied to each stage independently, exactly as the per-chip verdicts apply theirs to each chip. A stage that spans several chips is judged against one chip's tier, which is PESSIMISTIC, and it is disclosed rather than silently scaled by a chip count the schema does not tie to a stage.

D29 leaves the resident streams at DIFFERENT decode depths. Every priced attention and scan op uses ITS OWN stream's context — no op is priced at the representative figure. The representative context is the MEDIAN over the lowered window and exists so a reader can name the depth the reported state figures belong to. The convention is: stream i enters at prefill_len + i + 1 and advances one token every D beats.
